turns.en: Let's get you comfortable. This is your call bell, press it any time you need us. The bathroom's just through there.
turns.cy: Dewch i ni'ch gneud chi'n gyfforddus. Dyma'ch cloch alw chi — pwyswch hi unrhyw bryd dach chi angen ni. Mae'r stafell molchi jyst drwy fan'na.
chunks: Dewch i ni'ch gneud chi'n gyfforddus
press it any time you need us
pwyswch hi unrhyw bryd dach chi angen ni
Mae'r stafell molchi jyst drwy fan'na

turns.en: Lovely. Where shall I put my things? I've brought my own pillow.
turns.cy: Hyfryd. Lle wna i roi fy mhetha i? Dw i wedi dod â fy nghlustog fy hun.
chunks: kept distinct from Perfect → Perffaith, Grand → Campus, Good → Da iawn
Where shall I put my things?
Lle wna i roi fy mhetha i?
wna i for 'shall I' (R3); aspirate-mutated mhetha absorbed
Dw i wedi dod â fy nghlustog fy hun
Welsh 'bring' is the â-carrying frame dod â — the object is a prepositional complement

turns.en: Your things go in the cupboard there - and valuables are best going home with the family, if that's possible.
turns.cy: Mae'ch petha chi'n mynd i'r cwpwrdd fan'na — ac mae'n well i betha gwerthfawr fynd adra efo'r teulu, os ydy hynny'n bosib.
chunks: Your things go in the cupboard there
Mae'ch petha chi'n mynd i'r cwpwrdd fan'na
and valuables are best going home with the family
ac mae'n well i betha gwerthfawr fynd adra efo'r teulu
English's 'are best -ing' relocates to the mae'n well i + subject + verbal-noun frame

turns.en: Right you are. My son can take my rings home tonight, then.
turns.cy: O'r gorau. Mi fedar fy mab i fynd â fy modrwyau i adra heno, 'ta.
chunks: My son can take my rings home tonight
Mi fedar fy mab i fynd â fy modrwyau i adra heno
Welsh 'take' is the â-carrying frame mynd â, mirroring dod â for 'bring'

turns.en: Perfect. Anything you're not sure about, that's what the bell's for - don't sit there worrying quietly.
turns.cy: Perffaith. Unrhyw beth dach chi ddim yn siŵr amdano fo — dyna i be mae'r gloch. Peidiwch ag ista'n fan'na'n poeni'n ddistaw.
chunks: Unrhyw beth dach chi ddim yn siŵr amdano fo
HG25; 'anything' → unrhyw beth in the free-choice topic, against rhywbeth in offers — both live because neither is ever a free unit (S9)
the purpose-cleft frame dyna i be mae X (R3); y gloch feminine (R8)
Peidiwch ag ista'n fan'na'n poeni'n ddistaw
peidiwch ag before a vowel; the stacked yn-participles

turns.en: Thank you, bach. I feel better already.
turns.cy: Diolch, bach. Dw i'n teimlo'n well yn barod.
chunks: already Welsh in the canonical English — carried verbatim
Dw i'n teimlo'n well yn barod

turns.en: Let's get you settled. This is your call bell, and the bathroom's just through there.
turns.cy: Dewch i ni'ch setlo chi. Dyma'ch cloch alw chi, ac mae'r stafell molchi jyst drwy fan'na.
chunks: kept distinct from 'get you comfortable' → eich gneud chi'n gyfforddus
and the bathroom's just through there
ac mae'r stafell molchi jyst drwy fan'na

turns.en: What time's visiting? My husband wants to come this evening.
turns.cy: Faint o'r gloch ydy'r oriau ymweld? Mae fy ngŵr i isio dod heno.
chunks: Faint o'r gloch ydy'r oriau ymweld?
yr oriau ymweld is the one visiting-head course-wide (R7, S7)
My husband wants to come this evening
Mae fy ngŵr i isio dod heno
isio takes no linking yn — the northern want-frame

turns.en: Visiting's two till eight, so plenty of time. Two visitors at a time, that's the only rule.
turns.cy: Mae'r oriau ymweld o ddau tan wyth, felly digon o amser. Dau ymwelydd ar y tro — dyna'r unig reol.
chunks: Mae'r oriau ymweld o ddau tan wyth
masculine dau; the singular after a numeral

turns.en: Two till eight - I'll tell him. He finishes work at five, so that's perfect.
turns.cy: Dau tan wyth — mi ddeuda i wrtho fo. Mae o'n gorffen gwaith am bump, felly mae hynna'n berffaith.
chunks: the conjugated wrtho fo — 'tell' governs wrth, not a bare object
Mae o'n gorffen gwaith am bump
south: fe wedaf i / fe ddweda i

turns.en: Grand. And if you need anything at all before then, just press the bell.
turns.cy: Campus. Ac os dach chi angen rhywbeth o gwbl cyn hynny, pwyswch y gloch.
chunks: its own approval-word, distinct from Lovely/Perfect/Good
And if you need anything at all before then
Ac os dach chi angen rhywbeth o gwbl cyn hynny
'anything' → rhywbeth under the conditional; 'then' here is temporal hynny, not 'ta (S1)

turns.en: Let's get you comfortable. Press this bell any time you need us, day or night.
turns.cy: Dewch i ni'ch gneud chi'n gyfforddus. Pwyswch y gloch 'ma unrhyw bryd dach chi angen ni, ddydd neu nos.
chunks: Dewch i ni'ch gneud chi'n gyfforddus
Press this bell any time you need us
Pwyswch y gloch 'ma unrhyw bryd dach chi angen ni
the adverbial soft mutation on ddydd is absorbed

turns.en: I don't sleep well in strange places. Is it noisy at night?
turns.cy: Dw i ddim yn cysgu'n dda mewn llefydd diarth. Ydy hi'n swnllyd yn y nos?
chunks: I don't sleep well in strange places
Dw i ddim yn cysgu'n dda mewn llefydd diarth
diarth is the walk's one strange/unfamiliar lexeme (HG04)
Ydy hi'n swnllyd yn y nos?
Welsh's ambient 'it' is feminine hi, not the masculine o English's neuter would suggest

turns.en: It can get a bit busy some nights, I won't lie to you. But we keep the lights down, and you tell us if you can't sleep.
turns.cy: Mi fedar hi fynd braidd yn brysur ambell noson — ddeuda i ddim celwydd wrthach chi. Ond dan ni'n cadw'r gola'n isel, a deudwch chi wrthan ni os fedrwch chi ddim cysgu.
chunks: It can get a bit busy some nights
Mi fedar hi fynd braidd yn brysur ambell noson
HG28 verbatim; feminine hi for the ambient subject
ddeuda i ddim celwydd wrthach chi
Welsh has no verb 'to lie' here — it says 'I won't say a lie to you'
But we keep the lights down
Ond dan ni'n cadw'r gola'n isel
English's plural 'lights' erases into the Welsh collective gola
and you tell us if you can't sleep
a deudwch chi wrthan ni os fedrwch chi ddim cysgu
emphatic chi after the imperative carries English's fronted 'you'

turns.en: I might need something to help me sleep, in that case. Can I ask for that?
turns.cy: Ella bydd raid i mi gael rhywbeth i fy helpu i gysgu, 'ta. Ga i ofyn am hynny?
chunks: I might need something to help me sleep
Ella bydd raid i mi gael rhywbeth i fy helpu i gysgu
the modal relocation ella + bydd raid i mi, as in the opener
the permission ga i frame, distinct from ability fedra i

turns.en: You can, of course. I'll ask the doctor to write something up, just in case you need it.
turns.cy: Cewch, wrth gwrs. Mi ofynna i i'r doctor sgwennu rhywbeth i lawr, rhag ofn y byddwch chi ei angen o.
chunks: the verb-echo answer system: Welsh answers with the verb, never a pronoun-plus-auxiliary
I'll ask the doctor to write something up
Mi ofynna i i'r doctor sgwennu rhywbeth i lawr
gofyn i, then a bare verbal noun — no Welsh 'to'
just in case you need it
rhag ofn y byddwch chi ei angen o
the rhag blocking preposition; angen takes a possessive object, not a direct one

turns.en: Thank you. I feel better knowing that's there.
turns.cy: Diolch. Dw i'n teimlo'n well o wybod bod hynny yna.
chunks: I feel better knowing that's there
Dw i'n teimlo'n well o wybod bod hynny yna
English's bare participle relocates to the causal o + verbal noun, with a bod that-clause under it
